question.problem:
A group of randomly selected customers from a certain insurance company was asked about the type of vehicle driven and whether they received a speeding ticket in the last year. The results of the survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | SUV | Sport car | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Speeding ticket | $80$ | $5$ | $85$ |
| No speeding ticket | $20$ | $5$ | $25$ |
| Totals | $100$ | $10$ | $110$ |

There are $220$ drivers in another insurance company. Assuming that the distribution of the results is the same for both companies, estimate the number of drivers in the second insurance company that drive SUV or received a speeding ticket, but not both.

current_example.problem:
There are $250$ boys and $250$ girls in a school. Of them, $40$ boys and $40$ girls were randomly selected and asked which sport they prefer between volleyball, basketball, football, or soccer. The results of the survey are given in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Volleyball | Basketball | Football | Soccer | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Girl | $14$ | $10$ | $2$ | $14$ | $40$ |
| Boy | $8$ | $12$ | $11$ | $9$ | $40$ |
| Totals | $22$ | $22$ | $13$ | $23$ | $80$ |

Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student in the survey is a boy who prefers football or soccer, and then use this to estimate the number of students in the entire school who are boys that prefer football or soccer.
current_example.worked_solution:
To estimate the probability that a randomly selected student is a boy who prefers football or soccer, we

- add up the numbers at the intersection of the row **"Boy"** and the columns **"Football"** and **"Soccer"**, and then

- divide by the total number of data points in the table.

The numbers at the intersection of the row **"Boy"** and the columns **"Football"** and **"Soccer"** are highlighted in the table below.

|  | Volleyball | Basketball | Football | Soccer | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Girl | $14$ | $10$ | $2$ | $14$ | $40$ |
| Boy | $8$ | $12$ | $\color{blue}11$ | $\color{blue}9$ | $40$ |
| Totals | $22$ | $22$ | $13$ | $23$ | $80$ |

Adding up these numbers and then dividing by the total number of data points in the table $(80),$ we get

$$
p = \dfrac{11+9}{80} = \dfrac{20}{80} = 0.25.
$$

This represents the estimated probability that a randomly selected student is a boy who prefers football or soccer.

Finally, to estimate the number of students in the entire school who are boys that prefer football or soccer, we multiply the total number of students in the school $(500)$ by the probability above:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =500\cdot p \\  & =500\cdot 0.25 \\  & =125\end{aligned}
$$
